title: Acute Pulmonary Embolism
scenario: A 54-year-old female presents to the emergency department with sudden onset of sharp right-sided chest pain and shortness of breath that began 2 hours ago. She returned from a 12-hour international flight yesterday and reports left calf pain and swelling for the past two days.

lines: 54-year-old female presents with sudden dyspnea and pleuritic right-sided chest pain for 2 hours. Reports recent 12-hour flight and 2 days of left calf pain and swelling. Anxious and restless. Skin cool and pale. Left calf warm, erythematous, and tender to palpation with unilateral edema. Alert and oriented x3.
IV access obtained. Continuous cardiac monitoring and pulse oximetry applied. Supplemental oxygen initiated. Labs, ECG, and CT pulmonary angiogram ordered. Provider notified.
CT pulmonary angiogram confirms a large embolus in the right main pulmonary artery. Anticoagulation initiated per order. Client remains anxious; reassurance provided.
Reports breathing is easier and chest pain reduced. Skin warm and pink. Denies bleeding. Resting more comfortably.
Acetaminophen 500 mg PO as needed for pain
Titrate oxygen to maintain SpO2 greater than 94%
Initiate IV heparin infusion per weight-based protocol
Continuous cardiac and pulse oximetry monitoring
Draw aPTT 6 hours after heparin initiation and per protocol
Bed rest with head of bed elevated
Notify provider for SpO2 less than 90% or systolic B/P less than 90 mmHg

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.rationale: Hypoxia, tachypnea, tachycardia, and acute pleuritic chest pain are hallmark signs of acute pulmonary embolism and require prompt intervention. A mildly elevated temperature and normal orientation are not immediate concerns.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each finding, click to specify whether it supports a diagnosis of pulmonary embolism, deep vein thrombosis, or both. Each finding may support more than one condition.

rows.text: Sudden pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea
Unilateral left calf swelling and tenderness
SpO2 86% with respiratory alkalosis on ABG

children.rationale: Acute dyspnea, pleuritic pain, and hypoxia with respiratory alkalosis point to embolism in the lung; unilateral calf swelling and tenderness point to a lower-extremity clot. An elevated D-dimer is a nonspecific marker of clot breakdown and rises with either condition.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Complete the sentence. The nurse determines that the priority problem is {1}, and the most immediate goal is to {2}.
children.rationale: The embolus obstructs pulmonary blood flow, causing impaired gas exchange evidenced by hypoxia and tachypnea. Restoring adequate oxygenation is the most immediate, life-preserving goal and takes priority over pain and other concerns.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each intervention, click to specify whether it is indicated or contraindicated for this client at this time.

rows.text: Administer supplemental oxygen titrated to SpO2 greater than 94%
Elevate the head of the bed
Encourage early ambulation in the hallway

children.rationale: Oxygen, upright positioning, and anticoagulation address hypoxia and the underlying clot. Massaging the calf or ambulating can dislodge additional thrombus and are contraindicated during the acute phase.

children.subject: Pharmacology
children.stem: After initiating the IV heparin infusion, which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Assess for signs of bleeding such as bruising or hematuria
Ensure protamine sulfate is available as the reversal agent
Administer aspirin concurrently for added clot prevention
Encourage vigorous tooth brushing to maintain oral care

children.rationale: Heparin therapy requires aPTT monitoring, bleeding precautions, assessment for hemorrhage, and availability of protamine sulfate for reversal. Adding aspirin increases bleeding risk, and vigorous brushing can cause gum bleeding.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Which findings indicate that treatment has been effective? Select all that apply.

options.text: Reports reduced chest pain and easier breathing

children.rationale: Improved oxygenation, a slower respiratory rate and pulse, and reduced chest pain show gas exchange and perfusion are recovering. Persistently cool, pale skin would indicate ongoing poor perfusion, not improvement.
